narrative.whats_happened:
Calibre Financial's first call was a 90-minute governance deep-dive led by Nathan Cole, Data Governance Lead, and Yara Haddad, VP of Enterprise Data. A fourth, unidentified participant joined partway through and asked substantive questions throughout without ever introducing themselves.

The decisioning-boundary question — whether Apex ever makes autonomous judgments rather than executing customer-defined logic — got a clear, repeated, unambiguous answer that Nathan and Yara both explicitly accepted. Encryption and key-management mechanics were described in detail, but Nathan declined to call that resolved pending his own security team's validation. Vendor lock-in and cross-institution identity matching were both left genuinely open, the latter explicitly deferred as its own future conversation.

No economic buyer has engaged yet, and no next step was set. Yara was explicit that they need to loop in someone named Renata internally before this moves further.

stakeholders.name: Yara Haddad
stakeholders.title: VP, Enterprise Data
stakeholders.evidence: Can we get into the governance and access control side more directly now? I think that's going to be the thing that actually determines whether this is viable for us.

stakeholders.name: Nathan Cole
stakeholders.title: Data Governance Lead
stakeholders.evidence: I think — I think that's directionally right, but I'd want our security team to actually validate the specifics before I'd call it resolved.

stakeholders.name: Unidentified Speaker
stakeholders.evidence: Sorry, sorry — got pulled out of another call, didn't mean to walk in mid-sentence. Please continue, I'll catch up.

objections.text: Where does Apex's processing actually run — Calibre's environment or an Apex-controlled store
objections.resolution_note: Runs against Calibre's own warehouse. Nathan called this 'the right starting answer' but explicitly reserved further follow-up.

objections.text: Does Apex ever make autonomous decisioning judgments rather than executing logic Calibre defines
objections.resolution_note: No exceptions, including for risk. Nathan: 'that's actually the answer I needed to hear.' Yara confirmed the boundary is non-negotiable and got the answer she needed.

objections.text: Encryption, tokenization, and key-management mechanics for sensitive fields
objections.resolution_note: Detailed answer given, but Nathan explicitly declined to accept it as resolved pending his own security team's validation.

objections.text: How locked in would Calibre be, and does the export mechanism actually satisfy vendor-exit compliance obligations
objections.resolution_note: Tom explicitly could not answer the compliance-checklist version of this question and took it as a real follow-up item.

objections.text: Whether tokenization holds up for cross-institution matching against third-party-tokenized data
objections.resolution_note: Explicitly deferred as needing its own dedicated design conversation, not answered on this call.

objections.text: Latency and event-ordering guarantees for the risk-alerting use case specifically
objections.resolution_note: A substantive, specific answer was given (bounded lateness window, configurable per use case), but the unidentified speaker still wants a dedicated risk-architecture session before treating it as settled.

integration_patterns.description: Service-account access to Calibre's warehouse, scoped to specific schemas/views, reads broad-ish within scope and writes narrow to designated outputs, all logged
integration_patterns.caveats: Nathan explicitly reserves full validation for his security team; the deal has no committed next step, so nothing here is agreed in the full sense yet.

success_criteria.customer_words: say a customer's spending pattern suggests they might be a good fit for a product they don't currently have, or conversely, their behavior suggests early signs of financial distress that risk would want to know about. Today, neither of those signals reaches anyone in a timely way
success_criteria.interpreted: Wants real-time signals — product-fit opportunities and early financial-distress risk indicators — to reach the right internal team promptly, which today's siloed systems can't do.

product_relevance.need_stated: It's tracked, but not uniformly, honestly — retail banking has a reasonably mature consent framework, wealth management's is less mature, and I'd call risk's approach to permissible use more policy-based than systematized. / that unevenness is real, and it's honestly one of the things I'd want this to help us get in front of rather than just inherit.
product_relevance.relevant_release: Consent Sync — models consent and permissible-use state centrally and can surface coverage gaps rather than silently defaulting, directly addressing the cross-organization inconsistency Nathan and Yara described.
